questions.q: What is the dusty, loose soil covering the Moon called?
questions.fact: Moon regolith is sharp and clingy because no wind or water has smoothed its grains.

questions.q: About how much Moon rock did the Apollo missions bring back to Earth?
questions.fact: Scientists are still studying these samples today.

questions.q: About how many Earths could fit inside the Sun?
questions.fact: The Sun is about 109 times wider than Earth.

questions.q: About what percent of all the mass in the solar system is in the Sun?
questions.fact: All the planets, moons, asteroids and comets together make up only about 0.2 percent.

questions.q: About how hot is the center of the Sun?
questions.fact: The core is so hot and squeezed that hydrogen atoms fuse together.

questions.q: About how hot is the surface of the Sun?
questions.fact: That is hot enough to melt and boil any metal on Earth.

questions.q: About how many times wider is the Sun than Earth?
questions.fact: If the Sun were as tall as a front door, Earth would be about the size of a nickel.

questions.q: What is the roughly 11-year rise and fall in sunspots called?
questions.fact: At the peak of the solar cycle, there are more sunspots, solar flares and bright auroras.

questions.q: What is a solar flare?
choices: A ring of light around the Sun
A sudden burst of energy from the Sun
questions.fact: Big solar flares can disrupt radio signals and GPS on Earth.

questions.q: Which NASA spacecraft has flown closer to the Sun than any other?
questions.fact: In December 2024, Parker Solar Probe passed about 6.1 million kilometers from the Sun's surface.

questions.q: Which part of the Sun makes its energy?
questions.fact: Energy made in the core can take thousands of years or more to work its way out to the surface.

questions.q: Why should you never look straight at the Sun, even during a partial eclipse?
choices: It can permanently damage your eyes
questions.fact: Special eclipse glasses block almost all of the Sun's light so you can watch safely.

questions.q: What is the dark center of a shadow during an eclipse called?
questions.fact: The lighter outer part of the shadow is called the penumbra.

questions.q: On what date in 2024 did a total solar eclipse cross Mexico, the United States and Canada?
questions.fact: Millions of people watched as the Moon covered the Sun for up to about four minutes.

questions.q: What is an annular solar eclipse?
choices: When the Moon covers the Sun's middle but leaves a ring of light
When two moons cover the Sun
questions.fact: It happens when the Moon is a bit farther from Earth and looks too small to cover the Sun completely.

questions.q: What is the harvest moon?
choices: The full moon closest to the start of autumn
The last moon of the year
questions.fact: Long ago, its bright light helped farmers keep harvesting crops after sunset.

questions.q: About how long is one full day, from sunrise to sunrise, on the Moon?
questions.fact: So any spot on the Moon gets about two weeks of daylight followed by about two weeks of night.

questions.q: Why do temperatures on the Moon swing from very hot to very cold?
choices: It has no atmosphere to hold heat in
It is very close to the Sun
questions.fact: The Moon's surface can go from about 120 degrees Celsius in daylight to below minus 170 at night.

questions.q: How wide is the Moon compared to Earth?
questions.fact: The Moon is about 3,474 kilometers across.

questions.q: Where does Earth's Moon rank in size among all the moons in the solar system?
questions.fact: Only Ganymede, Titan, Callisto and Io are bigger.

questions.q: What are the bright streaks that spread out from some craters on the Moon called?
questions.fact: The crater Tycho has rays that stretch across much of the Moon.

questions.q: Which moon is slowly spiraling toward its planet and may break apart someday?
questions.fact: Mars's moon Phobos gets about 2 meters closer to Mars every 100 years.

questions.q: Which planet is often called Earth's twin because it is almost the same size?
questions.fact: Venus is about 95 percent as wide as Earth, but it is nothing like Earth on the surface.

questions.q: What are the clouds of Venus made of?
questions.fact: The thick clouds reflect so much sunlight that they make Venus shine brightly in our sky.

questions.q: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun?
questions.fact: Venus has a runaway greenhouse effect that keeps it at about 465 degrees Celsius day and night.

questions.q: About how hot is the surface of Venus?
questions.fact: That is hot enough to melt lead.

questions.q: The air pressure on Venus's surface is like being how deep in Earth's ocean?
questions.fact: The air on Venus is more than 90 times heavier than on Earth.

questions.q: Which Soviet spacecraft series sent back the first pictures from the surface of Venus?
questions.fact: Venera landers only lasted a short time before the heat and pressure destroyed them.

questions.q: Most features on Venus are named after whom?
questions.fact: Its tallest mountains, Maxwell Montes, are the main exception.

questions.q: Craters on Mercury are named after what kind of people?
questions.fact: Mercury has craters named after Beethoven and Mark Twain.

questions.q: What has been found in shadowy craters at Mercury's poles, even though Mercury is close to the Sun?
questions.fact: Sunlight never reaches the floors of these deep polar craters, so the ice never melts.

questions.q: Which spacecraft orbited Mercury from 2011 to 2015?
questions.fact: MESSENGER found evidence of water ice in Mercury's polar craters.

questions.q: What gas makes up most of Mars's thin atmosphere?
questions.fact: The air on Mars is about 100 times thinner than on Earth.

questions.q: What color are sunsets on Mars?
questions.fact: Fine dust in the Martian air scatters blue light near the Sun at sunset.

questions.q: What are Mars's polar ice caps made of?
choices: Water ice and frozen carbon dioxide
questions.fact: Frozen carbon dioxide is also called dry ice.

questions.q: How wide is Mars compared to Earth?
questions.fact: Mars is the second smallest planet after Mercury.

questions.q: Why does Mars sometimes seem to move backward across our sky?
choices: Earth is passing it as they both orbit
questions.fact: This is called retrograde motion, and it puzzled ancient astronomers.

questions.q: What was the famous Face on Mars photographed in 1976?
choices: A hill that looked like a face because of shadows
questions.fact: Later sharper photos showed it was just an ordinary mesa.

questions.q: Which spacecraft was the first to orbit Mars, in 1971?
questions.fact: Mariner 9 arrived during a planet-wide dust storm and had to wait for it to clear.

questions.q: In what year did NASA's Viking 1 land on Mars?
questions.fact: The Viking landers carried experiments to look for signs of life in the soil.

questions.q: Which NASA lander dug up water ice near Mars's north pole in 2008?
questions.fact: Phoenix scraped the soil and watched small chunks of ice slowly disappear.

questions.q: What did NASA's InSight lander mostly study?
choices: Marsquakes and the inside of Mars
questions.fact: InSight recorded more than 1,300 marsquakes.

questions.q: What is the name of the crater where the Perseverance rover landed?
questions.fact: Jezero Crater once held a lake, which makes it a good place to look for signs of ancient life.

questions.q: Which country reached Mars orbit on its very first try in 2014?
questions.fact: India's Mangalyaan mission cost less than many Hollywood space movies.

questions.q: What is the name of China's first Mars rover, which landed in 2021?
questions.fact: Zhurong is named after a fire god from Chinese myths.

questions.q: What are China's Chang'e Moon missions named after?
choices: A Moon goddess from Chinese legend
questions.fact: In the legend, Chang'e lives on the Moon with a jade rabbit, and China's Moon rovers are named Yutu, meaning jade rabbit.

questions.q: Who was China's first astronaut, in 2003?
questions.fact: China became the third country to launch a person into space on its own rocket.

questions.q: What are Russian astronauts called?
questions.fact: The word cosmonaut comes from Greek words meaning universe sailor.

questions.q: What does the word astronaut mean in Greek?
questions.fact: Astro means star and naut means sailor.

questions.q: Who was the commander of Apollo 13?
questions.fact: The story of Apollo 13 was made into a famous movie in 1995.

questions.q: What did the Apollo 13 crew radio to Mission Control after the explosion?
questions.fact: People often misquote it as Houston, we have a problem.

questions.q: What did Neil Armstrong say as he stepped onto the Moon?
choices: That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind
questions.fact: About 600 million people watched the landing on TV.

questions.q: What words are on the plaque left on the Moon by Apollo 11?
choices: We came in peace for all mankind
questions.fact: The plaque is attached to the leg of the lunar module's base, which stayed on the Moon.

questions.q: Which US president challenged America to land a person on the Moon before 1970?
questions.fact: He made the challenge in a speech to Congress in 1961.

questions.q: Which two countries competed in the Space Race?
questions.fact: The Space Race lasted from the late 1950s to the early 1970s.

questions.q: What were NASA's first seven astronauts called?
questions.fact: They were chosen in 1959 from a group of military test pilots.

questions.q: How many astronauts flew in each Gemini spacecraft?
questions.fact: Gemini is Latin for twins, a good name for a two-person spacecraft.

questions.q: How many astronauts flew on each Apollo Moon mission?
questions.fact: Two astronauts landed on the Moon while the third stayed in orbit.

questions.q: Which astronaut flew to space again in 1998 at the age of 77?
questions.fact: John Glenn had first orbited Earth 36 years earlier.

questions.q: Who was the first African American woman to travel to space?
questions.fact: Mae Jemison flew on the Space Shuttle Endeavour in 1992.

questions.q: Which NASA mathematician checked the orbit math for John Glenn's flight and was featured in the movie Hidden Figures?
questions.fact: John Glenn asked for her to check the computer's numbers before he would fly.

questions.q: Who led the team that wrote the software for the Apollo guidance computer?
questions.fact: A famous photo shows her standing next to a stack of code printouts as tall as she was.

questions.q: Which astronaut recorded a music video of the song Space Oddity on the International Space Station in 2013?
questions.fact: It was the first music video filmed in space.

questions.q: Which astronaut spent almost a year on the International Space Station while an identical twin stayed on Earth for a NASA study?
questions.fact: The study compared the twins to learn how long spaceflight changes the human body.

questions.q: Who holds the record for the longest single trip in space, as of 2025?
questions.fact: Valeri Polyakov spent about 437 days in a row on the Mir space station in the 1990s.

questions.q: Which American astronaut has spent the most total days in space, as of 2025?
questions.fact: As of 2025, Peggy Whitson has spent close to 700 days in space over several missions.

questions.q: Who wrote and hosted the famous 1980 TV series Cosmos?
questions.fact: Carl Sagan also helped choose what went on the Voyager golden records.

questions.q: Which scientist studied black holes and wrote the book A Brief History of Time?
questions.fact: Stephen Hawking predicted that black holes slowly give off a faint glow, now called Hawking radiation.

questions.q: Who is the Hubble Space Telescope named after?
questions.fact: Edwin Hubble proved that many fuzzy patches in the sky are whole other galaxies.

questions.q: What problem did the Hubble Space Telescope have right after launch?
choices: Its main mirror was slightly the wrong shape
It was in the wrong orbit
questions.fact: Astronauts fixed it in 1993 by adding corrective optics, like giving Hubble glasses.

questions.q: How many times did astronauts fly to the Hubble Space Telescope to fix and upgrade it?
questions.fact: The last servicing mission was in 2009.

questions.q: What did Hubble's famous Pillars of Creation picture show?
choices: Towers of gas and dust where stars are forming
questions.fact: The pillars are in the Eagle Nebula, about 6,500 light-years away.

questions.q: What did the Hubble Deep Field picture reveal in a tiny dark patch of sky?
questions.fact: Almost every speck of light in the picture is a whole galaxy, not a single star.

questions.q: Which NASA space telescope studies X-rays from very hot things like exploding stars?
questions.fact: X-rays from space are blocked by Earth's air, so X-ray telescopes must be in orbit.

questions.q: Which giant radio telescope in Puerto Rico collapsed in 2020?
questions.fact: Arecibo appeared in movies, including the James Bond film GoldenEye.

questions.q: Which country built FAST, the giant 500-meter-wide radio telescope?
questions.fact: FAST sits in a natural bowl-shaped valley.

questions.q: What do radio telescopes detect?
questions.fact: Radio telescopes can work during the day and even through clouds.

questions.q: Why are many big telescopes built on tall mountains?
choices: It is cheaper to build there
There is less air and cloud to blur the view
questions.fact: Many of the world's best telescopes sit high on mountains in Hawaii and Chile.

questions.q: What is a galaxy?
choices: A huge group of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity
questions.fact: Scientists estimate there are hundreds of billions of galaxies in the universe we can observe.

questions.q: About how many stars are in the Milky Way?
questions.fact: Most of these stars are too faint to see without a telescope.

questions.q: Which type of galaxy looks like a round or oval ball of stars?
questions.fact: Elliptical galaxies usually have older stars and little gas for making new ones.

questions.q: What are the two small galaxies, seen from the Southern Hemisphere, that are close neighbors of the Milky Way?
questions.fact: They are named after explorer Ferdinand Magellan, whose crew described them.

questions.q: What is dark matter?
choices: Unseen matter that scientists detect only by its gravity
questions.fact: Scientists think there is about five times more dark matter than regular matter.

questions.q: What is a quasar?
choices: The super bright center of a faraway galaxy powered by a black hole
questions.fact: Some quasars shine brighter than a trillion Suns.

questions.q: What is a white dwarf?
choices: The small, hot leftover core of a star like the Sun
questions.fact: A white dwarf is about the size of Earth but has about as much mass as the Sun.

questions.q: What is a brown dwarf?
choices: An object too big to be a planet but too small to be a true star
questions.fact: Brown dwarfs never got hot enough to fuse hydrogen like real stars.

questions.q: What is a neutron star?
choices: The super-dense core left behind after some supernovas
questions.fact: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.

questions.q: What makes stars seem to twinkle?
questions.fact: Seen from space, stars do not twinkle at all.

questions.q: What happens to the light from a galaxy that is moving away from us?
questions.fact: This is called redshift, and it helps scientists measure how fast galaxies are moving.

questions.q: What is the faint glow left over from the Big Bang called?
questions.fact: It was discovered by accident in 1965 by two scientists who first thought the signal came from pigeon droppings on their antenna.

questions.q: What did the LIGO detectors observe for the first time in 2015?
questions.fact: The waves came from two black holes crashing together more than a billion light-years away.

questions.q: About how cold is deep space, far from any star?
questions.fact: That is only a few degrees above absolute zero, the coldest temperature possible.

questions.q: Which planet is fifth from the Sun?
questions.fact: Between Mars and Jupiter lies the asteroid belt.

questions.q: Which planet lies between Saturn and Neptune?
questions.fact: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun.

questions.q: Which is the largest of the four rocky planets?
questions.fact: The rocky planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.

questions.q: What kind of planets are Jupiter and Saturn?
questions.fact: They are made mostly of hydrogen and helium, like the Sun.

questions.q: What are Uranus and Neptune often called?
questions.fact: They contain lots of water, ammonia and methane, which scientists call ices.

questions.q: What would happen if a spacecraft tried to land on Jupiter?
choices: There is no solid surface to land on
questions.fact: The gas just gets thicker and hotter the deeper you go, until it would crush any spacecraft.

questions.q: About how many times wider is Jupiter than Earth?
questions.fact: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

questions.q: What is the main gas in Jupiter's atmosphere?
questions.fact: Jupiter is about 90 percent hydrogen by number of molecules.

questions.q: What has been happening to Jupiter's Great Red Spot over the last hundred years?
choices: It moved to the north pole
questions.fact: Even though it has shrunk, the Great Red Spot is still wider than Earth.

questions.q: What was the Great Dark Spot seen by Voyager 2 in 1989?
questions.fact: When Hubble looked at Neptune a few years later, the spot had disappeared.

questions.q: Many of the moons of Uranus are named after characters from which writer's plays?
questions.fact: Uranus has moons named Miranda, Titania, Oberon and Juliet.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the Roman god of war?
questions.fact: Mars's red color reminded ancient people of blood and battle.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the fast messenger of the Roman gods?
questions.fact: The name fits, because Mercury is the fastest-moving planet.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the Roman goddess of love and beauty?
questions.fact: Venus is the only planet named after a female god.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the king of the Roman gods?
questions.fact: It is a good name for the biggest planet in the solar system.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the Roman god of the sea?
questions.fact: Its deep blue color makes the name fit well.

questions.q: Which planet is named after an ancient Greek god of the sky?
questions.fact: Uranus is the only planet named after a Greek god instead of a Roman one.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the Roman god of farming?
questions.fact: Saturday is also named after Saturn.

questions.q: Which is the widest dwarf planet?
questions.fact: Eris is a little smaller than Pluto but has a bit more mass.

questions.q: How many dwarf planets are officially recognized, as of 2025?
questions.fact: As of 2025, they are Ceres, Pluto, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.

questions.q: Which dwarf planet is stretched into an egg shape because it spins so fast?
questions.fact: Haumea spins once about every four hours, one of the fastest spins of any big object in the solar system.

questions.q: Which NASA spacecraft visited both the asteroid Vesta and the dwarf planet Ceres?
questions.fact: Dawn was the first spacecraft to orbit two different worlds beyond Earth.

questions.q: Which NASA mission brought back a sample from the asteroid Bennu in 2023?
questions.fact: The sample capsule parachuted down into the Utah desert.

questions.q: What did NASA's DART spacecraft do in 2022?
choices: Crashed into an asteroid to change its path
questions.fact: DART hit the small asteroid Dimorphos and successfully shortened its orbit.

questions.q: Which Japanese spacecraft brought back samples from the asteroid Ryugu?
questions.fact: Hayabusa means peregrine falcon in Japanese.

questions.q: Which asteroid will pass very close to Earth, even closer than some satellites, in April 2029?
questions.fact: Scientists have checked carefully, and Apophis will not hit Earth in 2029.

questions.q: What flattened about 80 million trees in Siberia in 1908?
choices: A space rock exploding in the air
questions.fact: This is called the Tunguska event, and the blast happened above the ground.

questions.q: In which country did a meteor explode over the city of Chelyabinsk in 2013?
questions.fact: The blast shattered windows across the city, and many people caught it on dashboard cameras.

questions.q: In which country is the Hoba meteorite, the largest single meteorite ever found?
questions.fact: The Hoba meteorite weighs about 60 tons and was never moved from where it landed.

questions.q: In which US state is the famous Meteor Crater?
questions.fact: Meteor Crater is about 1.2 kilometers wide and was made about 50,000 years ago.

questions.q: Why do scientists search for meteorites in Antarctica?
choices: Dark rocks are easy to spot on the white ice
It is warmer than other places
questions.fact: Moving ice also carries meteorites to certain spots, piling them up.

questions.q: Have meteorites from Mars been found on Earth?
choices: Yes, they were blasted off Mars by impacts
questions.fact: Scientists can tell they are from Mars because gas trapped inside matches the Martian air.

questions.q: Which comet was easy to see without a telescope for months in 1997?
questions.fact: Hale-Bopp was visible to the naked eye for about 18 months.

questions.q: Which comet broke into pieces and crashed into Jupiter in 1994?
questions.fact: Some of the impact scars on Jupiter were bigger than Earth.

questions.q: What are space junk and space debris?
choices: Old satellites and broken pieces orbiting Earth
questions.fact: Even a tiny paint chip can be dangerous because it moves faster than a bullet.

questions.q: What is special about a satellite in geostationary orbit?
choices: It stays above the same spot on Earth
questions.fact: Geostationary satellites orbit about 36,000 kilometers above the equator.

questions.q: About how fast must something go to escape Earth's gravity completely?
questions.fact: This speed is called escape velocity.

questions.q: About how high above Earth does space begin, by the most common definition?
questions.fact: This boundary is called the Karman line.

questions.q: What is the floating, weightless feeling that astronauts have in orbit called?
questions.fact: In microgravity, astronauts can push off a wall with one finger and float across a room.

questions.q: Why do astronauts on the International Space Station exercise about two hours a day?
choices: To keep their bones and muscles strong
questions.fact: Without gravity to push against, bones and muscles get weaker quickly.

questions.q: What happens to astronauts' height while they live in space?
questions.fact: Without gravity squeezing their spines, astronauts can grow a few centimeters taller, but it goes away back on Earth.

questions.q: How do astronauts sleep on the International Space Station?
choices: In sleeping bags attached to the wall
questions.fact: In microgravity there is no up or down, so sleeping on a wall feels the same as on a floor.

questions.q: What do astronauts often eat instead of bread, so crumbs do not float into equipment?
questions.fact: Floating crumbs could get into astronauts' eyes or clog machines.

questions.q: What does the International Space Station recycle into clean drinking water?
questions.fact: The station's system recycles about 98 percent of the water on board.

questions.q: What shape does a candle flame take in microgravity?
questions.fact: Without gravity, hot air does not rise, so the flame spreads out evenly in all directions.

questions.q: Why are spacesuits usually white?
choices: So they glow in the dark
To reflect sunlight and stay cooler
questions.fact: In direct sunlight in space, a dark suit would soak up too much heat.

questions.q: What is a spacewalk officially called?
questions.fact: Astronauts on spacewalks are tied to the station with safety tethers.

questions.q: What keeps a spacecraft from burning up when it comes back into Earth's air?
questions.fact: Reentry heats the outside of a capsule to well over 1,000 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: What were the first animals sent into space, in 1947?
questions.fact: The fruit flies rode on a V-2 rocket and came back alive.

questions.q: What was the name of the first chimpanzee to fly into space, in 1961?
questions.fact: Ham was trained to pull levers during the flight, proving that tasks could be done in space.

questions.q: What were the dogs Belka and Strelka famous for in 1960?
choices: Being the first dogs to orbit Earth and come back alive
Pulling a sled to the South Pole
questions.fact: One of Strelka's puppies was given as a gift to US President John F. Kennedy's family.

questions.q: What is the 1990 photo of Earth taken by Voyager 1 from about 6 billion kilometers away called?
questions.fact: In it, Earth is a tiny speck less than a pixel wide.

questions.q: What is the famous 1972 photo of the whole Earth, taken by the Apollo 17 crew, called?
questions.fact: It is one of the most shared photographs ever taken.

questions.q: How do scientists find many planets around other stars?
choices: By watching for stars to dim slightly when a planet passes in front
questions.fact: This is called the transit method, and the Kepler telescope used it to find thousands of planets.

questions.q: What is the habitable zone around a star?
choices: The area where it is the right temperature for liquid water
The part of a planet with cities
questions.fact: It is also nicknamed the Goldilocks zone, not too hot and not too cold.

questions.q: Which star system, announced in 2017, has seven Earth-sized planets?
questions.fact: Three of TRAPPIST-1's planets are in the zone where liquid water might exist.

questions.q: What is the line between day and night on a planet or moon called?
questions.fact: Craters near the terminator cast long shadows, so it is the best place to look at the Moon with a telescope.

questions.q: What is the point in the sky directly above your head called?
questions.fact: The point directly below you, through the Earth, is called the nadir.

questions.q: How much is Earth's axis tilted?
questions.fact: This tilt is the reason Earth has seasons.

questions.q: What causes Earth's seasons?
questions.fact: When your half of Earth tilts toward the Sun, sunlight hits more directly and it is summer.

questions.q: During which month is Earth closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, during winter in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.q: What is the day with the most hours of daylight in the year called?
questions.fact: In the Northern Hemisphere, it usually falls on June 20 or 21.

questions.q: What is special about an equinox?
choices: Day and night are about the same length everywhere
questions.fact: Equinox comes from Latin words meaning equal night.

questions.q: On average, which planet is closest to Earth?
questions.fact: Venus comes closest at times, but Mercury stays nearer on average because it never strays far from the Sun.

questions.q: Can the Great Wall of China be seen with the naked eye from the Moon?
questions.fact: The wall is very long but narrow, and from the Moon even whole continents look small.

questions.q: Which space agency is called ESA?
questions.fact: ESA has more than 20 member countries.

questions.q: What is India's space agency called?
questions.fact: ISRO stands for Indian Space Research Organisation.

questions.q: What is Japan's space agency called?
questions.fact: JAXA stands for Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.

questions.q: Which NASA center in Florida launches many rockets?
questions.fact: Apollo 11 launched from Kennedy Space Center in 1969.

questions.q: Which NASA center in Houston runs Mission Control for astronaut flights?
questions.fact: When astronauts radio Houston, they are talking to Mission Control there.

questions.q: What is the zone of orbits up to about 2,000 kilometers above Earth called?
questions.fact: Most satellites, and every human spaceflight except Apollo, have stayed in low Earth orbit.

questions.q: What was the name of the world's first space station, launched in 1971?
questions.fact: Salyut 1 was launched by the Soviet Union.
